about.title: Colfax Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Colfax sits where I-80 climbs toward the Sierra, and for a town of roughly 2,005 people, one lost life is felt on every street. Public records list 3 traffic deaths in Colfax for 2025, alongside 7 injury collisions that hurt 12 people. Most of those reports came from I-80 and its westbound lanes, S Auburn Street, and N Main Street. California law gives certain relatives — a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then specific dependents and heirs — the right to bring a wrongful death claim. That claim is civil, so it moves on its own track regardless of whether the CHP or the district attorney pursues charges. It can seek funeral and burial expenses, the income and support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. We handle these cases on a contingency basis, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. We can sort out who in your family holds that right before anything is filed.

items.title: The deadline is real
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a government entity is involved. Getting started early protects your options.

items.title: Every loss counts
items.desc: Funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one provided, and the loss of their companionship and guidance are all recognized under California law. We work on contingency, so there is no fee unless we recover for you.

items.question: My relative died in a crash on I-80 near Colfax. Where do I even start?
items.answer: Start by requesting the CHP collision report and keeping any hospital, funeral, and insurance paperwork together. Interstate crashes often involve out-of-area drivers or commercial carriers, which can complicate who is responsible. We can review the report with you and explain whether a wrongful death claim makes sense. Contact us at no cost.

items.question: The driver is being charged criminally. Do we still need a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes, they are separate matters. A criminal case is brought by the prosecutor and focuses on punishment; it does not pay your family's funeral costs or replace lost support. A wrongful death claim is a civil action that your family controls, and it can proceed whether or not charges are filed or result in a conviction.

items.question: How long do we have to act in California?
items.answer: The general deadline is two years from the date of death. If a city, county, or state agency may share fault — for example, a road maintenance issue — a formal government claim is usually required within a much shorter period. Because of that, it is wise to speak with an attorney sooner rather than later, even while you are still grieving.
